$comment: Closed set of semantic anchor roles. Owner of the type lists: story-bake (assets/story/roles.ts + anchors.ts resolve them, in Node and in the page). The role NAMES are a contract (schema enum, ROLE_IDS in assets/story/types.ts): adding or renaming one is a showrunner decision (reference/story/bake.md, 'Adding a role'). story-validator reads this file through anchors.ts to check that a beat's anchor (or one of its fallbacks) resolves in the beat's house. `items` are HouseSpec rooms[].items[].type values (the room's furniture); `siteItems` are lot items (spec.site[].type) that also answer an item role; `zones` are spec.site[].type values that answer a zone role. Every list is in preference order: the first type that exists in the house wins, then the next. The story-bake revision (same v: 1, additive) fixes the zone lists to the real spec vocabulary (the v1 seed named `garden` and `drive`, which no spec uses) and adds kindNames, home, siteItems and zoneRooms.

builtin.street: The public street in front of the lot. Always resolves (lot frontage).
builtin.front-door: The front door of the house. Always resolves (spec.entry / frontDoor).
builtin.core: The Companion Core (spec.hero). Always resolves. Its surface is a shelf or a desk; its room varies (see casting.json coreSpot).
builtin.room: The centre of the beat's room (use with anchor.room).

kindNames.living: living|lounge|family(?! bath)|salon|sunroom|reading|tv room|hearth|fireside|window bay|bay window|bay seat|picture window|\bden\b|library|games|garden nook|garden room|conservatory

universalNote: These resolve in all 30 homes. Every other role needs a fallback chain that ends in one of these, or the beat's house must be named in casting.json as having it. The validator fails a beat whose anchor and fallbacks all miss. `room` additionally needs anchor.room (and that room kind to exist in the house).
